ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus rishivalleyensis* is a small gecko (SVL ~40 mm) with a brown body featuring dark transverse bands. It is distinguished by its lack of precloacal pores and distinct, granular dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus rishivalleyensis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged, pale vertebral stripe that remains continuous and unbroken along the entire dorsum.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus rishivalleyensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn terrain within dry deciduous forests at elevations ranging from 700 to 900 meters.
ai.behavior: The Rishi Valley gecko is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small invertebrates among the leaf litter and rocky crevices of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus rishivalleyensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus rishivalleyensis* is endemic to the Rishi Valley in the Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh, India, occurring at elevations of approximately 700–800 meters.
